key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: The Governing Council today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: Over the medium term, consumption should be supported by gradually falling energy prices and a strong labour market.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: Inflation increased to 3.3 per cent in August, from 2.9 per cent in July.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: And we've also been surprised on the inflation front, because we have seen inflation, in a way, lower than we had anticipated.

briefing:
The ECB raised its key interest rates by 25 basis points. The Hawk & Dove stance index rates the press conference as slightly hawkish: it ranks at the 69th percentile of the 55 press conferences held since December 2019, up from the 56th percentile at the previous meeting on 23 July 2026. The monetary policy statement ranks at the 69th percentile and the answers in the Q&A at the 64th.

The ECB expects headline inflation to average 3.0 per cent in 2026, 2.5 per cent in 2027, and 2.1 per cent in 2028 [1]. The baseline projection for economic growth is 0.9 per cent for 2026, 1.4 per cent for 2027, and 1.5 per cent for 2028 [1]. The outlook remains highly uncertain, with risks to the upside for inflation and to the downside for economic growth [2].

A resurgence of trade tensions between major economies could further disrupt supply chains, reduce exports, and weaken consumption and investment [3]. The energy shock could intensify further and its effects on other prices and wages could be stronger than currently expected, driving up broader inflation through indirect and second-round effects [4].
